case_title: State of Rajasthan v. Mehram & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/land dispute: dispute over use of an unrecorded passage through the accused's fields; the victim's side had repeatedly entered those fields despite objections.
statutory_provisions: Charged/tried: IPC s.148, s.302, s.324/149 (accused No. 5 convicted at trial). High Court: s.326 IPC. Supreme Court: s.304 Part I and s.148 IPC.
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-5, 6, 7, 8, 11); medical (post-mortem and injury reports); recovery (blood-stained lathi, blood-stained clothing); spot inspection report and site plan
aggravating_circumstances: Accused were the aggressors, hid in bushes armed with lethal weapons and attacked on the complainant party's arrival; single fatal blow to the head with intention to kill.
mitigating_circumstances: Grave and sudden provocation from repeated unauthorised entry on the accused's fields; the provocation was not invited by the accused party; accused had simple injuries.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under ss.148, 302, 324/149 IPC; life imprisonment and Rs.100 fine for s.302; six months' simple imprisonment for s.148 and s.324/149 each.
high_court_outcome: Appeal partly allowed: s.302 conviction converted to s.326 IPC; s.148 conviction maintained; sentence reduced to period already undergone (about five months); Rs.50,000 compensation.
offence_finally_established: IPC s.304 Part I; IPC s.148
neutral_facts: A dispute existed between two family groups over use of an unrecorded passage that ran through fields owned by some of the accused and that the victim's group used to reach its own land. Earlier, a similar obstruction had been settled through local intervention. On the day of the incident, a quarrel broke out between a member of the victim's group and one of the accused over the passage, and the parties dispersed. At sunset, the complainant, a member of the victim's group, was walking alone towards the village when several men came out from behind a thicket of bushes near a pond and surrounded him. Some carried sharp-edged weapons and others carried sticks. One of the men allegedly swung a sharp-edged weapon at the complainant, who raised his hand and was wounded on the palm. Other members of the victim's group then arrived from their fields. One of them caught hold of the weapon, and the victim allegedly was struck on the head from behind with a sharp-edged weapon by one of the accused and fell. Beatings from both sides followed until other villagers intervened, after which the assailants ran away. The victim died of the head wound. Prosecution evidence included eyewitness depositions of several persons from the victim's group, the post-mortem report describing a deep incised wound to the head with the underlying bone and brain membranes cut, injury reports for both sides, the first information report lodged that night, a spot inspection memo and site plan, and recovery of a blood-stained lathi and blood-stained clothing of the injured and deceased.
offence_severity: Not stated for s.302 (charged offence). Judgment states that s.326 IPC carries imprisonment for life or up to ten years, and fine.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a single deep incised head wound (bone and brain membranes cut); complainant-side injury to palm; superficial injuries to accused No. 5.
number_of_offences: 3 charged against accused No. 5 (ss.148, 302, 324/149 IPC as convicted at trial); 2 finally upheld (s.304 Part I and s.148 IPC)
premeditation_planning: Court found accused had assembled with lethal weapons and waited in hiding for the complainant party to arrive; no separate finding of premeditated planning to kill.
motive: Court accepted: provocation from repeated unauthorised entry on the accused's fields. Trial court also found a revenge motive (alleged: revenge over the way dispute).
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-11 corroborated by PW-5, 6, 7, 8; post-mortem and injury reports; spot inspection report; recovery of blood-stained lathi and clothing; findings that accused were aggressors.
witness_credibility: Prosecution witnesses' evidence accepted as truthful by the trial court and not disturbed; Supreme Court found High Court's reasoning flawed when it departed from that evidence.
post_offence_conduct: Accused ran away after other villagers intervened (as recorded in the FIR and headnote).
custody_duration: Approximately five months (period already undergone per High Court sentence); exact custody period not stated.
bail_history: Bail bonds cancelled; accused directed to surrender within six weeks of relaxation of COVID-19 lockdown. Earlier bail grant or refusal not stated.
trial_duration: offence: 14.08.1981; trial judgment: 21.7.1982; High Court: 05.11.2007; Supreme Court: 06.05.2020
legal_representation: For State (appellant): Dr. Manish Singhvi, Sr. Adv., with D.K. Devesh and Milind Kumar. For accused (respondent): Sushil Kumar Jain, Sr. Adv., with H.D. Thanvi and Rishi Matoliya.
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; case committed to Sessions Court in February 1982; full trial completed with 14 prosecution witnesses.
procedural_irregularity: High Court's cryptic judgment applied a wrong assumption of provocation and private defence, and it imposed sentence for s.326 equal to time served; Supreme Court disapproved this approach.
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted ss.148, 302, 324/149 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: s.302 converted to s.326, sentence reduced to period undergone. Supreme Court: partly allowed; convicted s.304 Part I and s.148; 10 years' simple imprisonment.
prosecution_argument: State sought restoration of the s.302 conviction and life imprisonment for accused No. 5; appeal pursued against him only, on nature of offence and sentence.
defence_argument: Accused could challenge conviction without a formal appeal; incident was sudden due to provocation; blow was in private defence, so no intention to cause death; benefit of doubt; old age and health; if excessive private defence, benefit should go to accused.
legal_principle_applied: Where accused are aggressors, the right of private defence does not arise, so excess of private defence cannot be considered; s.300 exceptions (grave and sudden provocation) assessed to decide between s.304 Part I and Part II.
precedent_relied_upon: Chandrakant Patil v. State through CBI (1998) 3 SCC 38; Sumer Singh v. Surajbhan Singh (2014) 7 SCC 323; State of Rajasthan v. Ramanand (2017) 5 SCC 695 (accused's right to challenge conviction); Gottipulla Venkatasiva Subbrayanam (1970) 1 SCC 235, Deo Narain (1973) 1 SCC 347, Subramani (2002) 7 SCC 210, Gajey Singh (2009) 11 SCC 414 (cited by defence; Court did not dilate on them).
sentencing_rationale: High Court's sentence of about five months was inadequate given the nature and gravity of the offence and the background of the case; a ten-year term was imposed for s.304 Part I.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Grave and sudden provocation from repeated unauthorised entry on the accused's fields; provocation not invited by the accused party; single blow.
judicial_aggravating_factors: Fatal blow to a vital part of the victim's head with intention to cause death; accused was the aggressor; age plea rejected.
other_sentence_order: Compensation of Rs.50,000 to next of kin of deceased (if not already paid); set-off of period undergone under s.428 Cr.P.C.; bail bonds cancelled; surrender ordered.
